content_blocks.text: The pubspec.yaml File matters because Dart programs need predictable behavior, explicit contracts, and examples that can be verified. This topic focuses on package metadata, SDK constraints, dependencies, and development dependencies. Keep the lesson’s core distinction separate from runtime, SDK, package, or platform details that may vary. When you build on this idea, state your assumptions, try the smallest useful example, and check edge cases before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.text: Change one input or condition in the example for “The pubspec.yaml File”. Predict the output first, then run or statically inspect it. Add one boundary test and explain why the result is expected.

Common mistakes: confusing a language guarantee with a runtime or package behavior; skipping malformed/empty inputs; relying on undocumented version assumptions; and changing multiple things before reproducing a failure. Prefer explicit naming, a small test, and official documentation.
